newsitem.title: USA: Westin Hotels may sell or be publicly offered - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: Westin Hotels may sell or be publicly offered - WSJ.

text.p: An investment group led by Starwood Capital Group and Goldman Sachs & Co wants to sell Westin Hotels & Resorts for as much as $1 billion or more, the Wall Street Journal's electronic edition said Monday.
The report said potential bidders include Marriott International or a real estate investment trust controlled by Starwood.
Alternatively, the group may sell the Seattle-based chain of 102 hotels to the public through a stock offering, the report said.
"The situation is very fluid," Starwood Chief Executive Barry Sternlicht told the paper.
Westin is privately owned by Starwood Capital, Goldman Sachs' Whitehall real estate investment fund and members of senior Westin management, the report said.
